notice: Example path. Course names, numbers and examples come from Minerva's own pages as read on 18 Nov 2026; the short plain descriptions are ATLAS's. Cities and courses can change. Not admissions advice.

start.prompt: Which part of Minerva pulls you in?

options.label: Natural Sciences
options.whatYouDo: How the physical and living world works, from particles to planets.
facts: Physics lives here, as the Matter and Energy concentration. Minerva has no separate physics major.
options.keepsOpen: Four concentrations: Matter and Energy, Chemistry Across Scales, Cells and Organisms, Earth and Environmental Systems.

options.label: Computational Sciences
options.whatYouDo: Computation, mathematics and data as tools for hard problems.
facts: Math lives here, as the Mathematics concentration. Minerva has no separate math major.
options.keepsOpen: Five concentrations: Mathematics, Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, Data Science and Statistics, Applied Problem Solving, Contemporary Knowledge Discovery.

items: Formal Analyses (CS51): logic, statistics, algorithmic thinking
Empirical Analyses (NS51): framing problems, testing hypotheses, designing studies
Multimodal Communications: writing, speaking, visual design, debate
Complex Systems: collaboration, negotiation, leadership
y1-ns.note: Everyone takes these, alongside civic projects with San Francisco partners. Later courses list CS51 and NS51 as prerequisites.

y2-ns-elect.prompt: Your electives come from another major's core. Which one?

options.keepsOpen: The whole Matter and Energy track.

NS110L Physics of Life, NS111, NS112, NS113 Chemical Structure and Reactivity

y3-ns.stage: Year 3 · Focus · Buenos Aires and Europe
y3-ns.prompt: Pick a concentration. Your capstone starts this year too.

options.label: Matter and Energy
options.whatYouDo: The physics track: quantum mechanics, molecules, statistical mechanics.
facts: NS142 Quantum Nature of Matter: Theory and Applications (needs NS110U, CS111, CS113)
NS152 Analyzing Matter and Molecules
NS162 Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Applications (needs CS111)
options.keepsOpen: Physics-heavy graduate study and research.

options.label: Chemistry Across Scales
options.whatYouDo: Chemistry from molecules to cells to Earth systems.
facts: NS152 Analyzing Matter and Molecules
NS154 Life's Chemistry
NS156 Monitoring and Modeling Earth's Systems
options.keepsOpen: Shares NS152 with Matter and Energy, so the two sit close together.

options.label: More concentrations
options.whatYouDo: Two more: Cells and Organisms, and Earth and Environmental Systems.
facts: Students may also design a custom concentration with faculty guidance
options.keepsOpen: Year 3 electives can come from any concentration.

y3-ns-more.stage: Year 3 · Focus · Buenos Aires and Europe

options.label: Cells and Organisms
options.whatYouDo: How cells and organisms work, and what biotechnology can do with that.
facts: NS144 Genes to Organisms
NS154 Life's Chemistry
NS164 Solutions From and For Life
options.keepsOpen: Biology, health and biotech paths.

options.label: Earth and Environmental Systems
options.whatYouDo: How the atmosphere, land, oceans and life interact, and how we model change.
facts: NS146 Integrating Earth's Systems
NS156 Monitoring and Modeling Earth's Systems
NS166 Keeping Earth Habitable
options.keepsOpen: Climate and environment work; NS166 also counts toward the Sustainability minor.

y3-cs.stage: Year 3 · Focus · Buenos Aires and Europe
y3-cs.prompt: Pick a concentration. Your capstone starts this year too.

options.label: Mathematics
options.whatYouDo: Proof, analysis, and the math behind modeling.
facts: CS144 Real Analysis (needs CS114)
CS154 Analytical and Numerical Methods in Differential Equations
CS164 Optimization Methods
options.keepsOpen: Graduate study in math or theory, and quantitative roles.

options.label: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence
options.whatYouDo: What computers can do in principle, and building systems that do it.
facts: CS142 Theory of Computation
CS152 Theory and Applications of Artificial Intelligence
CS162 Software Engineering: Building Powerful Applications
options.keepsOpen: Software, AI and research paths.

options.label: More concentrations
options.whatYouDo: Three more: Data Science and Statistics, Applied Problem Solving, Contemporary Knowledge Discovery.
facts: Students may also design a custom concentration with faculty guidance
options.keepsOpen: Year 3 electives can come from any concentration.

y3-cs-more.stage: Year 3 · Focus · Buenos Aires and Europe

options.label: Data Science and Statistics
options.whatYouDo: Learning from data, and knowing when not to trust it.
facts: CS146 Computational Methods for Bayesian Statistics
CS156 Finding Patterns in Data with Machine Learning
CS166 Modeling and Analysis of Complex Systems
options.keepsOpen: Data work in almost any field.

options.label: Applied Problem Solving
options.whatYouDo: Computation and quantitative methods pointed at big real-world problems.
facts: CS162 Software Engineering
CS164 Optimization Methods
CS166 Modeling and Analysis of Complex Systems
options.keepsOpen: Engineering, product and startup paths.

options.label: Contemporary Knowledge Discovery
options.whatYouDo: AI, differential equations and machine learning together.
facts: CS152 Theory and Applications of Artificial Intelligence
CS154 Analytical and Numerical Methods in Differential Equations
CS156 Finding Patterns in Data with Machine Learning
options.keepsOpen: Research that mixes modeling and machine learning.

items: Finish your capstone, a sustained independent project begun in Year 3

Present your capstone at Manifest

options.label: Graduate study
options.whatYouDo: A master's or Ph.D., often in research.
facts: 43.5% of Natural Sciences graduates were pursuing an advanced degree six months out (n = 46, classes of 2019 to 2025)
Schools named: Harvard, Caltech, Cambridge, Karolinska Institute, Oxford, Johns Hopkins, Princeton
options.keepsOpen: Research, teaching, specialist science roles.

options.label: Work
options.whatYouDo: Straight into a job.
facts: 41.3% were employed full-time six months out (n = 46)
Industries: consulting and entrepreneurship 17.4%, education 15.2%, healthcare and biotech 6.5%
Roles named: researcher, lab technician, science consultant, computational biologist, bioinformatician
options.keepsOpen: Graduate study later, with work experience behind you.
